issues.legal_issue: An agreement providing for a future sublease after repayment of all amounts due does not create a landlord-and-tenant relationship before the sublease is executed, and a cooperative arbitration award for possession may be valid when the member defaults.
material_facts: A cooperative housing society advanced money for the plot premium and construction of a house, with repayment required in instalments.
The registered agreement provided that the society would grant a sublease only after the member paid all amounts due and fulfilled the agreement's conditions.
The member paid no instalments, and no sublease was executed.
The society referred the repayment and possession dispute to arbitration under the cooperative societies law, and the arbitrators awarded possession to the society.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was an executory contract, not a lease; no landlord-and-tenant relationship existed before execution of the sublease. The award was valid and was not barred by the rent-control law.
issues.legal_principle: The nature of a transaction is determined by construing the document as a whole, not by relying on a particular label used in it. Under sections 54 and 59 of the Bombay Co-operative Societies Act, 1925, the dispute could be referred to the cooperative arbitration process and the certified award could be executed. The rent-control law did not bar that process because no landlord-and-tenant relationship existed. The court did not apply Babulal Bhuramal v. Nandram Shivram to this issue.

rule.if: cooperative_society_dispute and agreement_promised_sublease_after_fulfillment and member_failed_to_pay_dues and sublease_not_executed

predicates.cooperative_society_dispute: A dispute arose between a cooperative society and its member in connection with the member's obligations to the society.
predicates.agreement_promised_sublease_after_fulfil: The agreement provided for a sublease only after the member fulfilled specified obligations, including paying the amounts due.
predicates.member_failed_to_pay_dues: The member failed to pay the amounts due under the agreement.
predicates.sublease_not_executed: The contemplated sublease had not been executed.

issues.definition: When a cooperative society's agreement makes a sublease conditional on fulfillment, the member fails to pay the dues, and no sublease has been executed, the society may obtain a valid cooperative award for possession without a landlord-and-tenant relationship.

issues.legal_issue: A party's plea that it is a tenant does not itself give the rent-control forum exclusive jurisdiction when the party seeking relief does not claim that a landlord-and-tenant relationship exists.
material_facts: The society sought possession on the basis of the member's persistent default and the society's right to terminate the agreement, rather than on the basis of a landlord-and-tenant relationship.
The member contended that the rent-control forum alone could decide the possession claim because the member was a tenant.
The society's claim before the arbitrators did not allege that the member was its tenant.
issues.conclusion: The member's tenancy plea did not displace the arbitrators' jurisdiction. Exclusive jurisdiction under section 28 depended on the proceeding being brought on a claim of a landlord-and-tenant relationship and seeking relief within that section.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, gives the designated court exclusive jurisdiction over proceedings between landlord and tenant relating to recovery of rent or possession of covered premises, and related claims or questions. The claim invoking jurisdiction must allege the landlord-and-tenant relationship; a defendant or respondent cannot displace ordinary jurisdiction merely by pleading that relationship. Babulal Bhuramal v. Nandram Shivram concerned a suit in which the plaintiffs themselves claimed to be tenants, and did not establish that an opposing party's plea alone suffices.

predicates.cooperative_arbitration_proceeding: The dispute was before an arbitrator appointed through a cooperative-society process.
predicates.claimant_sought_possession_on_non_tenanc: The party seeking possession relied on a basis other than a claimed landlord-and-tenant relationship.
predicates.opposing_party_alone_pleaded_tenancy: The party resisting possession, rather than the party seeking it, asserted that a landlord-and-tenant relationship existed.

issues.definition: When a cooperative arbitration proceeding seeks possession on a basis other than tenancy and only the opposing party pleads tenancy, that plea does not displace the ordinary adjudicative jurisdiction.
